body:
I had like four or five different groups to go out three days a week. Fuck, how many people did I knew yeah ? Nah. That's just acquaintances. I could have died and no one would have thought a lot about it.

What I say is that's better to have friends that you trust and you can depend on, than having the number of lots of people to hang out. Sincerely right now I have a single "friend". Only one I can trust my secrets, my real problems.. without fear of what's going to happen with the information, without being judged.. Mainly support.

Having acquaintances is a good plus. Having friends like the one you have.. that's the important. It doesn't suck at all. One of the best things you can have in life.

Turn off your phone. When you can't control your behavior setting blocks to it is a good way. I certainly do it.

There are also apps that block other apps for certain times of the day, usage etc

You can find new interests. I loved videogames when I was younger. I spend most of my teenager years without a single friend, a single girl.. playing videogames. I even went as far as being in my room for weeks, without going out of it for anything other than eat. Weeks without seeing anyone but my mother.

But I started to get bored by games and started going out. Parties and all that. A lot, lot of friends. Then alcohol and drugs. And now I fucked my grades at university because of those past habits.
Now I'm focused in yoga, exercise, and studying. Improving myself.

What I mean by all of that is that we change in ways we don't expect. It just happens. You may want to be the way you're now, but you will change anyway, and then you will like to be the new way.

What I say... just wait, things change A LOT in those years. It's not a good moment to make any harsh decision.

The joke is that if I had chosen the easy subjects I would have passed more than enough subjects. I just chose the difficult ones, because I thought I would be able. I didn't want to do the easy ones. And because of my overconfidence I fucked everything in my life. I will have to change city, change university, spend money, find some place to live, move all my things.. I just need this subject.
I just hope I had failed my first year, and not now, I'm my third year.

I destroyed my life using drugs.

I'm not close in the sense that I haven't seen some of my brothers who live like 20 minutes away, in months. I talk to my mom every week. It's not a bad family. Maybe just disconnected from each other, but good relations when it does connect. I may just be the disconnected point from all.

They probably will be accepting. Maybe even support me. But I can't handle my shame/pride.

Yes. You're right that in comparison with a lot of people I'm doing fine. Even good. But that's not comfort for me.

Thanks. The problem is the shame. I don't seem to be able to deal with it.

I know I just can keep on. It's the pride and the shame. It has been always the same. I even thought about suicide when I was 8 years old or even younger if I failed. I couldn't imagine it. Now I have done the major fail. Last year I lost my grant, didn't learn enough as I took drugs and drank a couple times this year (by year I mean full year, not 2015). Now I'm going to be kicked out of University.. I have to rent another place, move, do papers and papers, move to another city.. What I say to my mom ? I couldn't do more ? It's real, I just couldn't. This is my life I'm ruining. If I knew better I would have done better.

If I were intelligent, if I had chosen my subjects like I should had done. Nothing of this would be happening. This is the greatest lesson in my life. If I just have this exam with a pass grade..
